structured_output.title: Competitive brief on self-hosted AI agent platforms + landing page draft
structured_output.background: The owner wants two connected deliverables: (1) a one-page, source-backed competitive brief on self-hosted AI agent platforms, and (2) a landing page draft built directly from that brief. The company operates on the RosterDock board and has n8n engineering capability, so the implied context is positioning our own self-hosted AI agent/automation offering against the open-source and self-hostable field (e.g. n8n, Dify, Flowise, Langflow, Activepieces, Windmill, LangGraph/CrewAI-style frameworks, LibreChat/Open WebUI, Temporal-backed agent stacks). No product spec, ICP, or brand guide was supplied, so the requirements owner must state the assumed positioning and audience explicitly as flagged assumptions rather than block on them. Every factual claim that reaches the landing page must be traceable back to a cited source in the brief, since pricing, licensing (especially source-available vs. true OSS licenses) and competitor feature claims carry real risk. Research must be dated because this market changes monthly.
structured_output.outcome: A reviewable package: a dated competitor comparison matrix with sources, a one-page competitive brief distilled from it, a landing page content spec plus copy deck with claim-to-source traceability, and a working static landing page draft in the repository that renders the approved copy and contains no uncited claims.
structured_output.doneDefinition: Done when: (1) competitor-matrix.md covers at least 8 self-hosted AI agent platforms with license, deployment model, agent capabilities, pricing/limits, and a dated source URL per row; (2) competitive-brief.md fits one page (<=700 words) and every factual claim maps to a matrix source; (3) landing-page-spec.md and copy-deck.md define audience, positioning, final copy strings, CTAs, and a claim-to-source table with assumptions flagged; (4) a static landing page draft is committed to the repository, renders standalone in a browser at mobile and desktop widths, and uses only copy/claims from the approved spec; (5) the reviewer can verify each claim by following the cited link, with no dead references and no fabricated names or metrics.

tasks.title: Competitor matrix: self-hosted AI agent platforms (dated, sourced)
tasks.brief: Research and tabulate at least 8 self-hostable AI agent / agentic automation platforms. Suggested starting set (replace or extend with justification): n8n, Dify, Flowise, Langflow, Activepieces, Windmill, LangGraph self-hosted, CrewAI, Open WebUI or LibreChat, Rivet. For each row capture: product name, vendor, license (be precise: MIT/Apache-2.0 vs. source-available/fair-code/BSL and what it restricts), self-host deployment model (Docker, Helm/K8s, one-click), agent capabilities (tool/function calling, multi-agent, memory, RAG, human-in-the-loop), integration count, LLM/provider flexibility and local-model support, enterprise features gated behind paid tiers (SSO, RBAC, audit logs, air-gapped), pricing for self-hosted/enterprise, and observability. Add a GitHub stars / last-release-date snapshot for momentum. Every cell that states a fact needs a source URL plus the date accessed; prefer official docs, LICENSE files, pricing pages and repo releases over blog roundups. Mark unavailable information explicitly instead of guessing. Close with a 'gaps and whitespace' list: 3-6 substantiated observations about where the field is weak (governance, cost predictability, ops burden, compliance, upgrade risk).

criteria.text: At least 8 platforms covered with license, deployment model, agent capabilities, paid-tier gating and pricing columns filled or explicitly marked unavailable
Every factual cell has a working official source URL with access date; no dead links, no unsourced assertions
License classification is precise (true OSS vs. source-available/BSL) and momentum snapshot (stars, last release) is dated
Includes a 'gaps and whitespace' list of 3-6 substantiated market weaknesses

tasks.title: One-page competitive brief distilled from the matrix
tasks.brief: Write competitive-brief.md as a genuine one-pager: hard cap 700 words of body plus a compact numbered sources list. Structure: (1) dated market snapshot in 2-3 sentences; (2) segmentation of the field into 3-4 buyer-relevant clusters (workflow-automation-first, LLM-app/agent builders, chat-UI front ends, developer frameworks) with named examples; (3) a compressed comparison table, max 6 rows x 5 columns, showing only the axes a buyer decides on; (4) three to five differentiation openings we can credibly claim, each tied to a specific matrix gap; (5) two or three risks or counter-arguments a prospect will raise (license drift, ops burden, model cost, migration lock-in). Number every claim [1], [2]... resolving to URLs drawn from competitor-matrix.md. No adjective that cannot be substantiated; no competitor claim the cited source does not directly support. Add a short 'confidence notes' block outside the one-page body listing anything softened or uncertain and why.

criteria.text: Body is one page (<=700 words) and covers market snapshot, segmentation, compressed table, differentiation openings and risks
Every factual claim carries a numbered citation resolving to a matrix source, and each citation actually supports the claim
3-5 differentiation openings each trace to a specific gap identified in the matrix
Confidence notes block lists softened or uncertain claims

tasks.title: Landing page content spec, copy deck and claim traceability
tasks.brief: Turn competitive-brief.md into a build-ready spec (landing-page-spec.md) for a single marketing landing page for our self-hosted AI agent platform offering. Because no product spec or brand guide exists, open with an ASSUMPTIONS section stating the assumed primary and secondary audience, the assumed product promise, the single conversion goal and the primary CTA, each marked as an assumption the owner can cheaply overturn. Then specify, section by section: hero (H1 <=10 words, subhead <=25 words, primary and secondary CTA labels), problem framing, 3-4 differentiator cards taken from the brief's openings, a comparison block derived from the brief's table with explicit competitor-naming rules (only citable claims; prefer category language where the source is weak), objection handling covering license/ops/cost risks, a social-proof placeholder with substitution instructions, and closing CTA. Provide final literal copy, not directions. Include a claim-to-source table mapping every on-page factual statement to its brief citation number and URL, a REMOVE-BEFORE-PUBLISH placeholder list, and a page acceptance checklist (copy fidelity, responsive widths 360/768/1280, accessibility basics: heading order, alt text, AA contrast, focus states). Also produce copy-deck.md containing only the final strings keyed by section and element id so the engineer can paste without interpretation.

criteria.text: Assumptions section names audience, product promise, conversion goal and CTA, each explicitly flagged as an assumption
All specified sections present with final literal copy strings (not instructions), hero H1/subhead within length limits, mirrored in copy-deck.md by element id
Claim-to-source table maps every on-page factual statement to a brief citation and URL; nothing uncited survives
Includes REMOVE-BEFORE-PUBLISH placeholder list and an acceptance checklist covering responsiveness and accessibility basics

tasks.title: Build the static landing page draft from the spec
tasks.brief: Implement the landing page draft in the repository as a self-contained static page: index.html plus one stylesheet, no build step, no external CDN needed to render, system font stack. Use only the strings from copy-deck.md and the structure in landing-page-spec.md; do not invent, embellish or add competitor claims. Requirements: semantic HTML with correct heading order (exactly one h1), working in-page anchors for CTAs, accessible CTA buttons/form controls with visible focus states, alt text on every image or inline SVG, contrast meeting WCAG AA, responsive at 360px / 768px / 1280px with no horizontal scroll, and no analytics or third-party trackers. Render placeholders (logos, testimonials, metrics) as visibly marked PLACEHOLDER blocks matching the REMOVE-BEFORE-PUBLISH list, never as fake customer names or invented numbers. Add an HTML comment above each claim-bearing section referencing its citation number and source URL, and a README section explaining how to open the page, where copy comes from, which items are placeholders, and how claims are cited. Keep the diff focused on page, styles and README with no unrelated refactors.

criteria.text: Page renders standalone with no build step and matches the spec's section order and copy-deck strings verbatim
Responsive at 360/768/1280px with no horizontal scroll; semantic HTML with a single h1 and correct heading order
Accessibility basics satisfied (alt text, AA contrast, visible focus states) and no third-party trackers
Placeholders visibly marked per the REMOVE-BEFORE-PUBLISH list with no fabricated names or metrics; claims carry citation comments and README documents copy source
